messages:
rachel: Heads-up 5 opened a small PR to clarify athena8b model card: which quantized variants we serve, runtime fallback behavior, and a tiny client snippet to detect fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/521

maria: Thanks! Can you call out which quant variants are 'best-effort' vs fully supported? That helps support and sales messaging.

rachel: Good call. I added a short table: supported: float16, quant-int8; best-effort: quant-int4 (may fallback on older kernels). Also noted sequence_limit: 6144.

kevin: Can you include p50/p95 for a 512-token workload for both GPU and CPU fallback so customers understand the impact?

rachel: Added quick numbers: GPU p50 55ms p95 105ms; CPU fallback p50 320ms p95 760ms. Mentioned that longer contexts increase the CPU penalty.

ara: Please add a minimal SDK snippet showing how an app can detect fallback and retry or log it. Keep it one short code block.

rachel: Snippet added in the PR under "client detection":
```
# python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
r = c.generate("Explain the change", model="athena8b:quant-int4")
print(r.text)
if getattr(r, "runtime", "gpu") != "gpu":
    # runtime will be 'cpu' when fallback occurs
    log.warning("Fallback to %s for model %s", r.runtime, "athena8b:quant-int4")
    # optionally retry with a supported variant
    r2 = c.generate("Explain the change", model="athena8b:quant-int8")
    print(r2.text)
```

maria: Nit: use sentence case for headings and add a one-line migration checklist for Dedicated: verify pinned pools have updated kernels or schedule rolling upgrades.

rachel: Added a Dedicated checklist and a one-line Private deployment note (verify KMS and kernel version before rolling). Also fixed a stale anchor: /models/athena -> /catalog/athena8b.
